name: Sacral Insufficiency Fracture
definition: Fragility fracture of the sacrum resulting from normal physiological stress on weakened bone, commonly in older adults with osteoporosis.

typical: Often minimal or no trauma history

redFlags.item: Severe uncontrolled pain or inability to mobilize

investigations.principle: Plain radiographs may miss sacral insufficiency fractures.
investigations.MRI: MRI is highly sensitive and shows marrow edema; CT depicts fracture lines and healing.

amber: Persistent severe pain or unstable patterns require specialist assessment; sacroplasty is selective.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Bhagna/Asthi-kshaya principles may be considered only after modern fracture/stability assessment.

patientEducation.summary: Fragility fracture of the sacrum resulting from normal physiological stress on weakened bone, commonly in older adults with osteoporosis.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, breathing/swallowing difficulty, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
